chunks: And in it is that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except over those who follow him.
And He made for them partners in it to mislead them in knowledge. And for them is no knowledge of it, except they followed those who appeared [to have knowledge].

key_terms.الظَّاهِرِينَ: The apparent ones (those with outward knowledge/status)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the conditional nature of Satan's authority (*khud'*) over believers, emphasizing that it is not inherent but dependent on their voluntary submission to his whispers. This narration clarifies that those misled by false guides or superficial knowledge fall under this dominion, while true believers remain protected through divine grace. The context underscores the Shia theological principle that human free will determines the extent of Satan's influence, aligning with the verse in Surah Al-Hijr.
